title: CHSH bounds for contractions by dilation: Tsirelson's bound, the classical bound under a commuting party, and the necessity of noncommutativity
abstract: Kernel-checked transfer of the exact CHSH constants for self-adjoint involutions (Mathlib's IsCHSHTuple in a C*-normed ring: the norm of the CHSH operator T = A0 B0 + A0 B1 + A1 B0 - A1 B1 is at most 2*sqrt(2), equals 2 under a commuting party (the equality in a nontrivial real C*-normed algebra; the <= forms in every C*-normed ring), and exceeds 2 only if both parties are noncommuting) to self-adjoint CONTRACTIONS, together with the state corollary. A CHSH contraction tuple is four self-adjoint operators of norm at most 1 with the four cross-party commutations - IsCHSHTuple with the involution relations relaxed to norm bounds. The route is the Halmos dilation A -> A (x) Z + sqrt(1 - A^2) (x) X (Halmos 1950), applied with ONE ANCILLA PER OBSERVABLE: the four dilations form a Mathlib IsCHSHTuple on n (x) (C^2)^(x)4, every commutation relation among the four observables transfers to the dilations, the dilated CHSH operator compresses to T, and compression does not increase the operator norm, so every involution bound transfers. One ancilla per party would not do: for B0 = 1, B1 = 0 the single-ancilla dilations 1 (x) Z and 1 (x) X anticommute, so the commuting-party bound would not transfer. Nine compared statements: for n x n complex matrices (l2-operator norm), norm T <= 2*sqrt(2), norm T <= 2 if either party commutes, and 2 < norm T forces both parties noncommuting; for every density matrix rho, (1/2)|Re tr(rho T)| <= sqrt(2), and <= 1 under a commuting party; the same three norm bounds for bounded operators on a complete complex inner-product space (ampliation on the Hilbert sum WithLp 2 (E x E)); and, RESTATED, the parallelogram bound norm(A0 (B0 + B1) + A1 (B0 - B1)) <= 2*sqrt(2) for four operators of norm at most 1 with no self-adjointness and no commutation (folklore; formalized in Lean by Physical Superintelligence, 2026-10-23; proved independently here). The involution constants are the author's registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000007, re-proved here as library support and not compared. The bounds themselves are classical (Tsirelson 1980; the commuting-algebra bound as used by Summers and Werner 1987); new in this entry, relative to the Lean prior art recorded under sources (PSI's parallelogram and Hilbert-space state bounds; Lean-QIT's Kronecker-form state bound for contractions), are the contraction statements in the forms stated and their derivation from the involution constants by dilation (statements 1 and 6 are, as statements, the self-adjoint cross-commuting case of the parallelogram bound; their novelty is the route). The Challenge imports Mathlib only; the three structures it uses (IsCHSHContractionTuple for matrices, IsDensityMatrix, Hilbert.IsCHSHContractionTuple for operators) are verbatim copies of the library's, checked byte for byte by scripts/check_challenge_definitions.py. The Mathlib definitions the statements import (the scoped l2-operator norm on matrices, PosSemidef under ComplexOrder, IsSelfAdjoint and the adjoint, the trace, the operator norm, WithLp 2, IsCHSHTuple) are quoted verbatim from the pinned source with permalinks in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md and kernel-checked in DefinitionAudit.lean, a default build target that is not compared.
